commit.message:
fix(setup): admit only strict JSON for Claude Code configuration (#4944)

Claude Code shared the generic `json` client format, which the shared
configuration reader admits through JSONC parsing with comments and
trailing commas enabled. Native Claude Code reads `.claude.json` with a
strict JSON parser (after a UTF-8 BOM), so setup reported `ready`, wrote
a registration into a file the client rejects as corrupt, and doctor
reported it `aligned`.

Give Claude Code its own `claude_code` configuration format and parse it
at the owning boundary with strict JSON.parse after removing a leading
BOM. Setup, doctor, and uninstall all consume that parser, so comment or
trailing-comma documents are now refused as malformed before any backup
or write, while plain and BOM-prefixed JSON still configure. Clients that
natively accept JSONC keep the `json` format and its behavior.

Fixes #4940

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(tests): isolate command finalization module mocks

Move the five registered WASM finalization cases into the existing per-file isolated project. Preserve all result, exit-code, observation and cleanup assertions. A preloaded shared CLI graph reproduces three failures before the move; the isolated covered packet passes.

Fixes #4959

fix(tests): budget CLI coverage from parsed options

Use the pinned Vitest parser for coverage and shard flags. Keep ordinary CLI workers at 384 MiB and covered workers at the tested 512 MiB with unchanged concurrency. Retain complete coverage and add actual-config regressions for false, provider-only and spaced-shard options.

Validation: 27 focused cases; 16 covered cases with CLI preloaded; 5 docs checks; typecheck/lint; exact discovery of 1578 files. Measured covered control: 22.18s elapsed, 46.52s CPU, about 2.33 GiB sampled summed process-family RSS on macOS arm64. Full Linux CI pending. No runtime/device verification claimed.

Fixes #4960

fix(tests): inherit server identity deadline policy

Remove per-case ten-second overrides from MCP catalog and identity checks. Keep the suite-owned bounded ordinary and coverage deadlines, all assertions, and session cleanup.

Fixes #4967

fix(setup): edit the duplicate JSON member that clients read (#4957)

JSON.parse, JSONC parse, and native Claude Code keep the last duplicate
object member, and parseClientConfiguration therefore validates the last
one. The shared setup/uninstall serializer instead edited text through
jsonc-parser's modify and findNodeAtLocation, which select the first
matching member, so setup and uninstall on configurations with repeated
server tables or rea members wrote into a shadowed member and failed
readback.

Locate every JSON text edit by the effective (last) member in one place,
replacing the first-member modify path. Removing an effective member
that shadows an earlier duplicate would activate that duplicate, whatever
its ownership, so the serializer now returns a tagged shadowed_member
failure and setup and uninstall refuse before writing a backup or the
configuration.

Fixes #4952

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix(plist): ignore processing instructions between container members

Exclude processing-instruction nodes at the shared container-member owner
before dispatching plist tags. Keep strict syntax validation and scalar
content rules, with app-resolution and CLI/MCP evidence regressions.

Adapted from Mangolycheematcha's PR #4965, including its boundary controls.
Added built CLI/MCP coverage and verified container fixtures with plutil.

Fixes #4964

fix(adb): preserve command failure target identities

Keep the selected device, addressed file and actual host operand distinct
at the command owner. Parse known device and file diagnostics before
projection, including AOSP host write/read failures and exact snapshots.
Classify complete captured stderr before shortening display text, and
scan leading notices without expanding the capture into a line array.

Adapt Xinglan233's PR #4655 and extend its source-shaped host controls.
Add built CLI/MCP identity, long-path, recovery and input-preservation
coverage. Real platform-tools and Android devices remain unverified.

Fixes #4641
Fixes #4643
Fixes #5051

Co-authored-by: 星闌 <xinglan233@163.com>

fix(native): retain signature roots until descriptor cleanup completes

Give each signature snapshot a private child-resource scope. Its composite
root lease closes those children before removing the directory and retains
both stages across failed retries. Bind local cleanup failures to their
exact owner so child release cannot clear a failed root removal.

Replace the mixed-outcome regression that expected premature root removal.
Cover real descriptor denial, primary/cancellation preservation, MCP close
and same-connection recovery. Expose underlying real codesign test errors
before asserting result fields.

Fixes #5052

fix(native): validate LLDB readback encoding before reporting facts

Decode completed journal rows strictly while retaining valid neighbors and torn-tail semantics. Preserve structured result read, decoding, JSON and schema failures through the typed fallback.

Fixes #5055

fix(native): retain UI interruption source through final cleanup

Record caller cancellation versus the owned deadline once and share that provenance through helper execution, scenario waits and finalization. Preserve independent failures and partial reports, consolidate scenario failure handling and dispose listeners on every exit.

Fixes #5056

fix(native): bound LLDB PID reads before validation

Derive the read limit from the accepted safe decimal PID plus a tolerated CRLF and overflow sentinel. Retain short-read handling, cached valid facts and existing descriptor ownership and handshake semantics.

Fixes #5057

fix(errors): retain secondary failures without replacing primary causes

Give the typed error owner a separate retained secondary-failure collection. Preserve exact direct causes, including caller cancellation reasons and absent causes, while keeping existing diagnostic and live cleanup ownership projections.

Fixes #5059

fix(native): retain LLDB evidence prefixes after read failures

Return byte prefixes with tagged read outcomes and exact causes. Share those facts across partial journals and captures, preserve typed primary failures and successful siblings, and keep zero-byte failures unavailable. Retain failed descriptor and root owners through retry.

Fixes #5058

fix(plist): preserve source semantics in XML data decoding

Adapt the completed-quartet decoder from PR #4981 at 4cf6cac14. Bind raw source spans to validated DOM nodes before entity and line-ending interpretation can change data bytes. Preserve depth preflight, reject invalid data forms and allocate exact decoded output through one shared quartet grammar.

Fixes #4978

Co-authored-by: Avichal Pandey <avichal2018lko@gmail.com>

fix(plist)!: preserve unknown XML scalar identities

Interpret complete scalar source at the XML owner instead of accepting numeric prefixes, permissive date strings or nonempty booleans. Retain malformed content as explicit unknown scalars with original literals and reasons, while preserving the surrounding archive and independent numeric facts.

Share the representation across plist, keyed archive, Interface Builder and entitlement projection; remove the superseded numeric fallback and helpers. Parse date fields as UTC, retain real entity/CDATA semantics, and distinguish native integer/real whitespace without ambiguous whitespace backtracking.

Validation: 276 source tests and 60 compiled/public tests passed, with updated scalar regressions rerun; static, architecture and docs checks passed. Native macOS plutil controls and CLI/MCP source-hash/time-zone controls executed. No Linux/Windows or deep-provider qualification. Tiny completed CLI task costs recorded; no performance improvement claimed.

BREAKING CHANGE: Unresolved XML scalar values now use $plist_type unknown wrappers with element, literal and reason. This replaces the former real/null unknown marker and malformed scalar prefix fallback. Supported extended UTC years now preserve their timestamp.

Fixes #4852

fix(session): align call relationship discovery with traversal modes

Declare the missing trace composition and correct call graph prerequisites to require address resolution plus the selected relationship direction. Report forward/backward modes and the actual default independently, preserving missing operations, owner failure reasons and direct partial outcomes.

Share the direction-to-provider mapping across runtime and discovery, reuse the mode evaluator, select defaults by name, and check composition coverage against every canonical enhanced contract. Keep same-endpoint traces callable without relationship reads.

Adapt the missing trace-composition correction proposed in PR #4729 and complete the directly related ownership/refactoring and sibling graph correction.

Validation: 75 source tests and 76 public MCP/schema tests passed; full static/architecture checks, docs and test discovery passed. Controlled SDK/provider workflows verified unchanged catalogs and normalized traces. Small whole-session costs were recorded, with no speedup claim. No native-engine, CLI, Linux/Windows or model tool-selection qualification.

Fixes #4687
Fixes #5068
Co-authored-by: AHMED <aptech356@gmail.com>

fix(session): admit direct native dispatch metadata providers

Share named metadata source operations between execution and capability discovery. Preserve symbol fallback and typed runtime failure behavior, and cover availability through public MCP workflows.

Fixes #5070

fix(apktool)!: select numeric regions using Android b+ qualifiers

Normalize three-digit region aliases at the shared locale owner, preserving
caller labels and physical-table reuse. Reject malformed legacy qualifiers
through the same CLI/MCP contract and table classifier.

Adapt the owner correction and regressions from PR #4918 after checking Android
and supported Apktool qualifier sources. Add public MCP validation and preserve
existing two-letter regional selectors.

Fixes #4916

BREAKING CHANGE: Numeric legacy locale selectors such as es-r419 are rejected.
Use es-419 or b+es+419. Two-letter region selectors remain supported.

Co-authored-by: Mert Kaya <47145541+mertkayacs@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(session): describe native UI trace source routes

Share source operations with execution owners and derive availability and missing prerequisites from one evaluation. Distinguish authored UI dispatch from native-seed call tracing without inventing a default request mode. Preserve target gates, typed failures and partial results.

Fixes #5071

test(contracts): align plist and UI finalization regressions

Update public-boundary expectations after the explicit XML unknown-scalar
and native UI deadline provenance changes. Retain raw malformed literals,
independent exact integers, expanded-year ISO dates, and partial UI reports.
Assert successful cleanup releases its lease and failed cleanup retains it
until close retries. Keep malformed-input and true date-range coverage.

The shared number fixture owns CLI/filesystem/MCP expectations. Native
plutil controls confirm integer entities are invalid plist literals, even
though they are valid XML. No runtime behavior or CI gates change.

Validation: 187 source cases, 138 focused public cases, final 97-case
rerun after fixture typing/group changes, full static/architecture checks,
and test discovery (1591 files).

fix(uninstall): preflight repeated registration ownership

Read shadowed registrations from the effective JSONC syntax tree before
any client is changed. Share the same typed ownership decision with the
reread before removal, including foreign OpenCode V1 fallbacks. Remove
all admitted duplicates using one member/separator planner and grant
serializer authority only for exact admitted paths.

Setup may remove its explicitly superseded OpenCode V1 path. Preserve
inactive repeated parents, unrelated entries, comments and source backups.
Use the pinned JSONC scanner instead of handwritten string decoding.

Validation: final 86 focused cases and 9 setup acceptance cases passed;
104 additional filesystem consumer cases passed. Static/architecture,
docs and discovery checks passed. A broader 186-case run had one OMP
timeout; its isolated 9-case rerun passed, with timeout cause unverified.
Controlled compiled CLI comparisons verify removal/refusal and backups;
real developer-client execution remains unverified.

Adapted from #4977 at 4cd22d4ec2f6ec9e6c8ebf98bf97e1d9d7f8ac23.
Closes #4976

Co-authored-by: Nikhil Bhagat <knewboy.nykhil@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(native): retain partial call routes and omitted sites

Separate enumeration outcome from retained facts in the native call-route
owner. Keep every available typed call with its source provider and site,
supplement incomplete kinds with inferred fallback targets, and retain
known routes when fallback fails. Per-reference unknowns take precedence
over aggregate availability; cancellation remains terminal.

Project partial routes before enumeration failures, preserve each omitted
route's relation, and include its call site in the omitted-edge identity
so distinct observations to one target cannot overwrite each other.
Remove the superseded success-only provider/result representation.

Validation: 69 focused cases plus final 30-case rerun, including nine
public SDK MCP regressions; full static/architecture, docs and discovery
checks pass. Controlled-provider source REDs reproduce both route loss
and omitted-site collisions. Real native providers remain unverified.

Closes #5073
Closes #3922
Closes #5128

Add the environment-manifest view kind to inspect_analysis_view for retained
HAR Evidence: the primary origin's recorded request lines become a
deterministic tool surface (names, path templates, parameters with their
rule and basis, observed query names, value-free body shapes, record
pointers), with excluded groups, three fixed unknowns and the shared
projection budget. The four format rules always apply; after-uid-literal,
opaque-token and sibling-variance are opt-in and labelled, and literal

* fix(analysis-view): bound body, route and name work in the environment manifest

Addresses the automated review findings on the PR: read request bodies at the
top level only instead of walking nested values; admit every literal route
part before materializing it; compare at most 32 segments in sibling-variance
and say so; keep stop words literal after a uid literal; keep the next
collision suffix per tool-name base; preserve a templated exclusion when two
groups print the same row.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): keep manifest folding, naming and media-type reads linear

Addresses the second automated review round: fold literal siblings through
set membership, key collision suffixes by the truncated name they share, and
charge a request media type before it is scanned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): charge the manifest group key before building it

Addresses the third automated review round: the composite key copies the
method, origin, template and rules, so that copy is reserved before the key
is stringified.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): accept a +json suffix only on application media types

Addresses the fourth automated review round: `image/example+json` or
`text/example+json` no longer counts as JSON for origin selection, exclusion
or body shapes, matching the documented `application/json` and
`application/*+json` contract.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): require the capture parent's exact subject for a manifest

Addresses the fifth automated review round: the manifest cites the report
path and digest, so a parent whose subject is absent or names another path or
SHA-256 is refused at admission, as the capture view already does; the
api-surface view keeps its existing admission.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): share truncated suffix allocation work

Track suffix progress by the actual truncated prefix and suffix width. Distinct full names can collide only after suffix truncation; sharing that progress prevents quadratic rescanning while preserving shorter free names and existing allocation order.

Co-authored-by: Kaoru0822 <208281322+kaoru0822-kitauji@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(analysis-view): merge only identifier-like siblings under sibling-variance

Addresses the sixth automated review finding: a bucket merged whenever one
literal carried a digit, folding plain words such as `mine` into the
parameter. The rule now partitions the bucket, merges the identifier-like
siblings and leaves the other literals as their own tools.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analysis-view): combine qualifying sibling cohorts

Keep coded identifiers and a qualifying plural hyphenated cohort in one eligibility Set before checking the minimum merge size. Read each literal once and reuse the same membership at the consumer, preserving non-identifier routes and the three-hyphen minimum.

Co-authored-by: Kaoru0822 <208281322+kaoru0822-kitauji@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs(analysis-view): clarify opt-in sibling folding

State the additional sibling-variance selection in the guide, acceptance specification and MCP parameter description. Preserve the existing single-rule behavior and caller-selected inference rules.

commit.message: docs(manifest): align plan with top-level body parsing

fix(native): preserve partial call reference evidence

Retain provider-reported call sites and raw classification independently of generic reference flags. Keep all endpoint evidence when containing-procedure routes merge, and include relation in edge identity to avoid order-dependent labels.

Closes #5130

fix(uninstall): retain per-file partial outcomes

Preserve configuration paths and constituent actions independently of aggregate status. Derive summaries from all leaf outcomes, including after final cleanup reporting, so a later failure cannot hide an earlier removal.

Closes #5079

fix(domain): preserve partial reference comparison facts

Own endpoint identity and per-edge kind knowledge in one parsed reference
representation. Preserve exact same-artifact coordinates and cross-artifact
name uncertainty, including generated and nonunique procedure labels.

Use exact multiplicity-preserving sparse compatibility flow instead of
positional/greedy pairing or a quadratic adjacency matrix. Share the native
coordinate parser with call paths and remove the superseded projections.

Validate public MCP comparison/reconstruction outcomes, independent tiny
permutation oracles, dense matching and advertised JSON Schemas.

Fixes #4210
Fixes #5131

Co-authored-by: Henglie <ebhenglie@gmail.com>

fix(investigation): scope automatic unknowns to result Evidence

Construct automatic unknown identity once at the application boundary.
Validate the original question before adding immutable Evidence scope, and
preserve each result's supporting link through CLI and MCP producers.

Apply the shared policy to derived investigations, managed comparisons and
verification, composed workflow residuals, and process-capture residuals.
This prevents registry conflicts and silent loss of later result links.
Keep explicit creation/update semantics and exact Evidence replays intact.

Cover all affected producer families with public MCP regressions, preserve
snapshot provenance distinctions, and retain blank-question/error handling.
Remove the superseded single-result call-path test.

Fixes #3333

Co-authored-by: Dragolone <160818051+Dragolone@users.noreply.github.com>

@@ -69,3 +69,11 @@ When the connected schema advertises `include_query_parameter_names`, select
 it in the view for distinct observed names with original record ordinals. Query
 values are omitted; the names establish neither required parameters nor a
 complete server schema. Keep the original parent Evidence for exact URLs.
+
+Use `inspect_analysis_view` with `view: {kind: "environment-manifest"}` on the
+same retained HAR Evidence to project the primary origin's request lines into
+named tools with path templates, parameters, observed query names, value-free
+body shapes and record pointers for an agent environment. Opt into
+`template_rules` only when recorded identifiers need them; every template,
+parameter and merged sibling is an inference, no header, cookie or body value is
+copied, and the three stated unknowns stay unresolved.

@@ -1,5 +1,93 @@
 # Changelog
 
+## [6.7.0](https://github.com/morluto/rea/compare/rea-agents-6.6.0...rea-agents-6.7.0) (2026-10-18)
+
+### Highlights
+
+- Client configuration edits follow the duplicate-member semantics used by MCP clients.
+
+### Changes
+
+- Includes the [6.6.0 changes and migration notes](https://github.com/morluto/rea/releases/tag/rea-agents-6.6.0). That version was tagged but was not published to npm.
+
+### Fixes
+
+- **Client configuration:** Setup edits the last repeated JSON/JSONC member, matching the value clients actually read. Setup and uninstall refuse a removal that would reactivate a shadowed duplicate, preserving the original configuration. ([#4957](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4957), [morluto/rea#4952](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4952)). Thanks @kaoru0822-kitauji, @xu91102.
+
+Full contribution record: [4 commits and 1 merged PR](https://github.com/morluto/rea/blob/rea-agents-6.7.0/docs/releases/6.7.0.contributions.json).
+
+## [6.6.0](https://github.com/morluto/rea/compare/rea-agents-6.5.0...rea-agents-6.6.0) (2026-10-18)
+
+### Highlights
+
+- Add Kuna as a caller-supplied static-analysis provider.
+- Query selected JavaScript facts and multiple APK locale tables without repeating the underlying analysis.
+- Extend Ghidra analysis to Windows ARM PE targets and explicit raw m68k images.
+- Preserve completed Evidence, cancellation reasons and retryable cleanup across provider and CLI finalization.
+
+### Changes
+
+- **Kuna analysis:** Use a caller-installed Kuna for procedure listings, pseudocode, assembly, call relationships, exact-address xrefs and cached string searches. Project exports retain source spans and digests; repeated requests reuse completed work. Recorded real-provider coverage uses Kuna 1.833 on Linux; Windows, PE and universal Mach-O are unsupported. See [the provider guide](docs/kuna-provider.md). ([#3832](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3832), [#3854](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3854), [#4071](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4071), [#4095](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4095)). Thanks @gensokyo-dev, @kaoru0822-kitauji, @N0zoM1z0.
+- **Retained JavaScript facts:** Query exact application paths, selected properties and filtered module references through `inspect_analysis_view`, with paging and complete row Evidence. These views reuse completed analysis and preserve source selection and unknown coverage. ([#4265](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4265), [morluto/rea#4190](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4190), [#4097](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4097), [morluto/rea#4092](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4092)). Thanks @kaoru0822-kitauji, @N0zoM1z0.
+- **APK locale tables:** Request several resource locales in one decode with repeatable CLI `--locales` or MCP `locales`. Each table reports its status and coverage; existing single-locale fields remain available. ([#4804](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4804), [morluto/rea#4777](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4777)). Thanks @abhay-2108, @N0zoM1z0.
+- **Windows ARM binaries:** Ghidra admits ARMNT/Thumb-2 and ARM64 PE applications and DLLs on the Windows x64 host lane. Recorded Ghidra 12.1.4 verification uses `WindowsResourceReference` disabled and raised startup budgets; default-analyzer completion, ARM64EC/ARM64X and Windows-on-Arm hosts remain unverified or unsupported. See [the exact scope](docs/windows-ghidra-p0.md#native-authority-and-target-identity). ([#3965](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3965), [morluto/rea#2186](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/2186)). Thanks @N0zoM1z0, @WestLabsAI.
+- **Raw m68k images:** Analyze explicitly selected big-endian m68k raw binaries using Ghidra’s fixed 68000 profile and a caller-supplied aligned entry. Real CLI/MCP verification used Ghidra 12.1.4 on macOS arm64; Linux is unverified and Windows P0 does not admit m68k. See [mapping requirements](docs/raw-binary.md). ([#4018](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4018)). Thanks @icedac.
+- **JADX deadlines:** Set `REA_JADX_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS` to extend APK loading and upstream operation deadlines together. Doctor reports the effective value and setup forwards an explicit selection. ([#4466](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4466), [morluto/rea#3918](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/3918)). Thanks @jaychou813, @SandstromPL.
+- **Electron window options:** Resolve stable local constant `BrowserWindow` options while retaining source provenance. Relevant writes and escapes keep the result unknown. ([#4400](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4400), [morluto/rea#4366](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4366)). Thanks @kaoru0822-kitauji, @N0zoM1z0.
+- **Language editions:** Add the Greek website edition and Malayalam documentation, with Korean typography and translation corrections across the site. ([#3520](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3520), [#4792](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4792), [#3821](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3821), [morluto/rea#3820](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/3820), [#3799](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3799), [morluto/rea#3798](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/3798), [#4344](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4344), [#3856](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3856), [#4166](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4166)). Thanks @gensokyo-dev, @hi2242, @kalayciburak, @kaoru0822-kitauji, @kraken-503, @kukinghan, @N0zoM1z0, @yeseong0412.
+
+### Fixes
+
+- **Cancellation and cleanup:** Keep completed observations, exact cancellation reasons and the original physical failure through finalization. Failed cleanup retains its process or file owner for retry; recovered resources disappear from pending-cleanup reports without replacing the original error. ([#4238](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4238), [morluto/rea#4232](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4232), [#4274](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4274), [morluto/rea#3923](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/3923), [3e82366](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/3e8236639abffa39deb5d5e939ec8baf6aaf3ca3), [16924e2](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/16924e275e939d0543ba01493324959a9e1d731c), [bbfe6ed](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/bbfe6edd60290f9bfbec68c8a0bcf605d8bbf5b3), [1f23e97](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/1f23e977b50301e91f02a4a17c9f8d48bb7b60f3), [08fbeb8](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/08fbeb8bdab27118b6c57039aef7c0fa8b6463bc)). Thanks @coygeek.
+- **Provider startup:** Join prerequisite probes and in-flight readiness work before shutdown, preserve typed timeout and JVM-memory failures, and retain startup diagnostics through cleanup. Ghidra recognizes keg-only Homebrew JDKs and names the setting responsible for a startup timeout. ([376eeca](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/376eeca770820b31f7f8d4c5fcc397315621643e), [ceeff5a](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/ceeff5a41788e47e5aee96a4baf191a6ce7fde4b), [3ad1032](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/3ad1032b11edea2dcb054e78f951cc43159ae83d), [964decd](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/964decd989acfa84c4bfc3295362c4c46877fc20), [3fa972a](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/3fa972af7c7cb6cf014ffc426bdf7130dc6f2fd2), [#4557](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4557), [morluto/rea#4556](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4556), [#4590](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4590), [morluto/rea#4241](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4241)). Thanks @DanielCvz1, @J0UH, @Rinkia, @RishTheFish21, @vadlachary2002.
+- **Client configuration:** Preserve the selected launcher, destination file, caller timeout choices and unresolved configuration evidence. Setup/uninstall recovery stays bound to the exact published file, keeps current verified backups, and transfers failed cleanup ownership for retry. ([d0253c9](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/d0253c99d65afbbd12732a2fdaf711640574e17f), [7e4eed9](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/7e4eed9dd48485b6a7100300aa98401811c2deb9), [2fb5e20](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/2fb5e204a35723f6f843d56ca47b0db94d8fcc44), [8235210](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/823521085a28f825e7fee1929d852d420042d1f7), [d818c3d](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/d818c3d2639d3115edb8a5269a754101aea6c3bd), [19329e4](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/19329e43bb38ca9d64512d801b25abcb188d2512), [dadf909](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/dadf909dce2e8b3d055541de69b4118d21276316), [333e0ab](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/333e0ab0dfc126a9915907d5079ed6195190e38e), [c15c206](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/c15c2062ad815cc9a3222ccfaeb7ef53cacd8b72)). Thanks @Adolanium.
+- **Configuration formats:** Read signed 64-bit TOML integers without rounding, handle large TOML documents without argument-spread failures, preserve JSONC trivia and Hermes YAML scalar text, and reject NUL bytes in registration environment values. ([#4937](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4937), [morluto/rea#4917](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4917), [c43bc0b](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/c43bc0bf66a4e245a0cafa40def0d0207bcbd73c), [4fd28fc](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/4fd28fc9e0c4f8358147af38c72ab9e814f52d61), [#3568](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3568), [#4335](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4335)). Thanks @alfredo1491, @gensokyo-dev, @kaoru0822-kitauji, @N0zoM1z0, @ShuaixinHuang, @xu91102.
+- **Claude Code configuration:** Setup, doctor and uninstall now accept only the strict JSON format Claude Code reads, including a leading UTF-8 BOM. Comments and trailing commas are refused before backup or writing; clients that support JSONC retain their existing behavior. ([#4944](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4944), [morluto/rea#4940](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4940)). Thanks @kaoru0822-kitauji, @xu91102.
+- **CLI output and dispatch:** Accept `--flag=value` and spaced global output values, keep array positions in filtered JSON, validate integer tokens before coercion, and exit quietly when the output reader closes. Cancellation remains effective through command finalization; app bundles and static native inspections select the intended workflow. ([#3811](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3811), [#4823](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4823), [2ae4e16](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/2ae4e1608f290c95ff7cff28c4d16a79b301d03d), [8d82579](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/8d8257928bbe8d43fedffc4db5fca26c8108820f), [#3781](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3781), [279c590](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/279c590ef6bb737d4a48ea696a0ae5eb30010b3d), [#3511](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/3511), [morluto/rea#3321](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/3321), [f31b231](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/f31b231a92a61be6bd1800b16be0b3210ae82944)). Thanks @arjunprabhulal, @coygeek, @kaoru0822-kitauji, @ShuaixinHuang, @Sriram-PR, @Tapraj-Pathak.
+- **Updates:** Route `--update` through the verified updater and bound retained package-manager diagnostics. ([4f7b5fb](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/4f7b5fb6023ce2ec449561782d09e3c7e5ac7c7b), [01cdbbd](https://github.com/morluto/rea/commit/01cdbbdc556262c47d04a5b3391dd9c17946d3fc)).

+# Environment manifest view from web network captures
+
+Issue: https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4933
+
+## Outcome
+
+`inspect_analysis_view` accepts `view: {"kind": "environment-manifest"}` for
+retained HAR Evidence and projects the primary origin's recorded request lines
+into a replayable tool surface: deterministic tool names, path templates,
+parameters, observed query names, value-free body shapes, status and
+content-type sets and record pointers, with excluded groups, three fixed
+unknowns and the shared projection representation budget. This increment adds
+the view kind only; serving and exporting an agent environment from the
+manifest are later increments.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- Accept only `inspect_web_network_capture` HAR parents; refuse native
+  mitmproxy, SAZ and qlog parents, and parents whose Evidence does not record
+  `sensitive_value_count: 0`, with the same typed unsupported errors as the
+  api-surface view.
+- Without opt-in rules, every tool template must equal the api-surface template
+  of the same group; the four format rules always apply with `basis: inferred`.
+- Apply `after-uid-literal`, `opaque-token` and `sibling-variance` only when
+  listed, each at most once, in that order. With `sibling-variance` selected,
+  fold literal siblings within its comparison scope into existing opt-in
+  parameters unless they are stop words, whichever was recorded first. With only
+  `opaque-token`, a non-opaque literal remains a separate tool. Never fold a
+  literal into a format-rule parameter or template a stop word;
+  `sibling-variance` compares routes of at most 32 segments and the manifest
+  states when a route exceeded that.
+- Derive tool names from the method and route literals deterministically, at
+  most 60 characters, unique within one manifest.
+- Derive `body_shape` for `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` from the tool's earliest
+  record when it carries a JSON-typed request body, as top-level key types
+  only without walking nested values; copy no header, cookie, query or body
+  value anywhere in the result.
+- List records as pointers (`ordinal`, `method`, `path`, `status`,
+  `content_type`) and excluded groups with reason `other-origin`,
+  `ui-page-or-asset` or `non-json`.
+- Mark the Evidence inferred whenever any tool or excluded group is templated,
+  derived otherwise; keep the parent's authority.
+- Admit the capture clone, the inline envelope, every retained pointer, group,
+  route part, observed value, query name and body-shape key before allocation,
+  and charge body parsing as temporary bytes, within the existing 96 MiB budget.
+
+## Acceptance and limits
+
+A source-owned Grafana-shaped HAR fixture (28 recorded exchanges on two
+origins) drives domain, service, MCP, CLI and acceptance coverage. Without
+rules the templates equal the api-surface grouping; with all three rules the
+fixture yields `/api/dashboards/uid/{uid}`, `/api/folders/{uid}` folding
+`general`, `/api/plugins/{plugin_id}/settings` and
+`/api/datasources/uid/{uid}/health`. A published contract example is
+reproduced byte-for-byte from fixture bytes through the real decoder and view
+service. The view performs no network activity and replays nothing; it does
+not establish handler identity, schemas, authorization or state transitions.
+
+## Deferred issue criteria
+
+Serving a manifest over streamable HTTP, exporting an agent environment from a
+manifest and the hosted verification lane are later independent increments of
+#4933. This PR must reference rather than close the whole issue.

+## Environment manifest
+
+Pass retained HAR Evidence to `inspect_analysis_view` with
+`view: {"kind":"environment-manifest"}` to project one application's recorded
+request lines into a replayable tool surface: the environment manifest that an
+agent environment later serves from retained Evidence. The view reuses the
+api-surface grouping, then keeps the groups on the primary origin, the origin
+with the most JSON-like records (`application/json`, `application/*+json`,
+`text/plain`, `text/markdown`), whose path starts with `/api/` or `/apis/` or
+whose content types are JSON-like. Every other group is listed under
+`excluded` with reason `other-origin`, `ui-page-or-asset` or `non-json`, and
+retained records without a usable request line are counted in a limitation.
+
+```json
+{
+  "name": "inspect_analysis_view",
+  "arguments": {
+    "source": { "kind": "retained-evidence", "evidence_id": "ev_..." },
+    "view": {
+      "kind": "environment-manifest",
+      "template_rules": [
+        "after-uid-literal",
+        "opaque-token",
+        "sibling-variance"
+      ],
+      "include_query_parameter_names": true
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+`origin` and `name` identify the environment; the name is the kebab-case
+primary host with dots and ports replaced by hyphens, `grafana-example` for
+`http://grafana.example`. Each tool carries a deterministic `name`, `method`,
+`path_template`, `api_surface_template` (the four-rule template of its
+earliest record), `params`, `query_parameter_names`, `body_shape`,
+`statuses`, `content_types` and `record_ordinals`. `records` lists one pointer
+`{ordinal, method, path, status, content_type}` per record a tool cites and
+never a header, cookie or body. Tools sort by template then method.
+
+Without `template_rules`, every `path_template` equals the api-surface
+template and `params` carry the four format rules with names `id`, `uuid`,
+`hash` and `date`; a repeated name gets a numeric suffix. Opt-in rules apply
+only when listed, each at most once (a repeated rule is an `invalid_request`),
+in this order:
+
+| Rule                | Applies to                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Parameter                                       |
+| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
+| `after-uid-literal` | The literal segment right after a literal `uid`, unless it is a stop word                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | `uid`                                           |
+| `opaque-token`      | A lowercase alphanumeric segment of twelve or more characters mixing letters and digits that is not a `v1`-style version                                                                                                                                                                        | `uid`                                           |
+| `sibling-variance`  | Groups equal in method, origin and segment count that differ in one literal at index 2 or later; the siblings whose literal is identifier-like (a digit or `:`, or three or more hyphenated names under a plural literal) merge, never a stop word, and the other literals stay their own tools | singular previous literal plus `_id`, else `id` |
+
+With `sibling-variance` selected, literal siblings within its comparison scope
+fold into existing opt-in parameters as observed values unless they are stop words.
+For example, select both `opaque-token` and `sibling-variance` so
+`/api/folders/{uid}` lists `general` beside the recorded token. With only
+`opaque-token`, `/api/folders/general` stays a separate literal tool.
+A position templated by one of the four format rules
+absorbs no literal, so `/api/teams/{numeric}` keeps its exact-format meaning
+and `/api/teams/search` stays its own tool. Opt-in placeholders use the
+parameter name; format-rule placeholders keep their api-surface spelling. Tool names are
+`<method>_<literals>` with `api`, `apis`, `namespaces`, `default`, `v`-prefixed
+version tokens and a `uid` literal before a parameter dropped, dotted literals
+cut to their first label, `_by_<params>` appended when parameters exist,
+sanitized to `[a-z0-9_]`, at most 60 characters and made unique with numeric
+suffixes: `get_dashboards_by_uid`, `get_plugins_settings_by_plugin_id`.
+
+`sibling-variance` compares routes of at most 32 segments; longer routes keep
+their grouped templates and the manifest says so in a limitation. `body_shape`
+is derived for `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` from the tool's earliest record when it
+carries an `application/json` or `application/*+json` request body: top-level
+keys and their JSON type names, never values and never nested structure; a body
+on a later record adds nothing. `unknowns` always states three facts: the authorization model, response
+semantics and state transitions are not established by a capture.
+`templated_groups` counts tools and excluded groups with a templated segment;
+whenever it is nonzero the Evidence is inferred, otherwise derived. The view
+performs no network activity and replays nothing. Native mitmproxy, SAZ and
+qlog captures, and parents inspected with `sensitive_values`, return the same
+typed unsupported errors as the api-surface view, including the canonical
+token `sensitive_values_unretained`.
+
+The manifest accumulator shares the api-surface admission model: the capture
+clone, the inline envelope, record pointers, groups, every route part, observed
+values, query names and body-shape keys are admitted before allocation, and each
+recorded body is charged as temporary bytes before it is parsed. Retained state and
+temporary work must fit together within the 96 MiB projection representation
+budget; exceeding it returns `resource_constraint` without a partial manifest.
+

+# Apktool shared decoding and table-only projection
+
+The measured question is the same in every comparison: inspect an APK's
+metadata/manifest and its default, German and Brazilian Portuguese string tables.
+One existing batch removes repeated decoding. An optional table-only projection
+then removes repeated primary strings without changing the selected facts.
+
+This is a static resource-query measurement, not an agent evaluation or a claim
+about reconstructing an application's behavior. The machine-readable measured
+summary is [apktool-string-tables.json](apktool-string-tables.json).
+
+## Revisions, inputs and execution
+
+- Baseline: `8f7d12e30d63f3d3b4cfe2a90336362841438f56`, latest main at issue start.
+- Projection source: `406af90023a545fb280601bf51f445e122c36378`.
+- Existing shared decode: [#4777](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4777),
+  integrated by [#4804](https://github.com/morluto/rea/pull/4804).
+- Projection follow-up: [#4982](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4982).
+- Linux x86-64, kernel 6.1.0-53-cloud-amd64, Node 24.18.0, npm 11.16.0,
+  Temurin 21.0.12.1, Apktool 3.0.3. The selected JAR's closeout digest is
+  `dbf930b076c6b9be08d57c449cacefc3bdd6b71ebd59b3066fc0e1f5b14f9423`;
+  decoder contents were not independently hashed for every request.
+
+- [newpipe](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/releases/tag/v0.29.1): 11,507,122 bytes; SHA-256 `18447bfb1e06d113edc88df93f471827280de06f6f3d4dc42f56f28b9c1bab79`. Valid projected counts: 1126/833/779; unsupported entries: 1/1/1.
+- [apidemos](https://github.com/appium/android-apidemos/releases/tag/v6.0.18): 6,521,217 bytes; SHA-256 `a9eecf37b26cd084855c530db81c2bb1b91f4c1b095a04f47aa7c20e2791f686`. Valid projected counts: 967/29/29; unsupported entries: 8/0/0.
+- [settings](https://github.com/appium/io.appium.settings/releases/tag/v8.2.1): 3,099,589 bytes; SHA-256 `e4024b3ee348929252bcaf5eb422bcab9e4ace96703499a84f3332281c03375f`. Valid projected counts: 25/19/19; unsupported entries: 0/0/0.
+
+The counts are default/de/pt-BR respectively. Source paths, XML digests, exact
+caller paths, runtime hashes and per-run identities/costs are in the JSON summary.
+The APKs were never installed or executed. Input digests were checked before and
+after each completed task; provider-owned workspaces were confirmed absent.
+
+Each task uses a fresh production stdio MCP runtime, complete paginated tool
+discovery, client inspection, resource call(s), `close_binary`, transport close
+and owned cleanup. OS file caches were not flushed. Every decode has a fresh JVM,
+APK snapshot, framework directory and workspace: these are not warm retained
+engine/database queries, nor cold-disk measurements.
+
+Tasks run serially on one logical CPU, with an 8 GiB family hard limit, 7 GiB
+early stop and no swap. Admission requires 16 GiB host availability; running
+tasks stop below 8 GiB host availability. CPU and kernel `memory.peak` cover
+the complete owned cgroup, including subprocesses, observer and file cache.
+Counters are captured at payload exit while the observer is alive; disappeared
+final whole-scope counters remain unknown. All completed payload receipts show
+successful owned cleanup and zero observed OOM/limit events at that checkpoint.
+
+## Correctness and owning change
+
+Separate native decodes were retained for independent Python Expat validation.
+It checks direct string entries, source entity spelling, unsupported markup
+counts, ordering and emitted prefixes against the XML bytes. Manifest text and
+package identity are checked separately. All six serial/batch pairs agree on
+selected strings, manifest, metadata and target identity. All nine projection
+pairs additionally preserve table counts and coverage; batch/table-only counts
+and coverage match the XML oracle. This qualifies REA's projection of these
+native outputs, not independent binary ARSC decoder completeness.
+
+The existing default batch repeats its primary table in top-level `strings` and
+`string_tables[0]`. On NewPipe this made the full resource replies larger than
+three serial replies despite reducing decode calls: 616,059 → 680,188 bytes.
+ApiDemos' larger common manifest produces the opposite tradeoff. The existing
+batch remains the compatibility default.
+
+`string_tables_only: true` (CLI `--string-tables-only`) keeps the complete
+requested table facts inline in `string_tables` and leaves `strings` empty by
+request. An unrequested field does not establish that a source table is empty.
+This also supports one table without `locales`. `include_strings: false` still
+suppresses string projection. Omitting the new option preserves old requests:
+three real legacy workflows produce identical complete MCP replies, including
+Evidence identity, at the new source revision.
+
+The resource projection owner computes the output choice and charges aggregate
+entries for the copies actually emitted. The same 10,000-entry policy can thus
+return five distinct 2,000-entry tables rather than consuming capacity on a
+duplicate primary copy. Per-table limits, XML budgets, physical alias reuse,
+coverage, partial observations and cancellation remain at the existing owner.
+CLI and MCP share this implementation; there is no new tool or cross-call cache.
+
+## Existing shared decode: three serial calls versus one batch
+
+Three alternating fresh-session pairs per APK, all at the same main revision.
+The table reports marginal medians; paired speedups are reported separately.
+Elapsed/CPU include discovery, client/Java startup, calls, transcript/hash checks
+and cleanup. Native oracle creation, tokenization and verification gates are
+separate costs in the JSON, not hidden inside these task timings.
+
+| Target   | Resource calls, s | Whole elapsed, s |  Whole CPU, s | Family peak, MiB |
+| -------- | ----------------: | ---------------: | ------------: | ---------------: |
+| newpipe  |      23.19 → 7.40 |    35.32 → 19.86 | 34.95 → 19.65 |  1341.7 → 1309.5 |
+| apidemos |      17.43 → 6.22 |    30.32 → 18.85 | 30.05 → 18.63 |  1187.1 → 1202.7 |
+
+Paired resource-call speedup medians: NewPipe **3.23×** (2.90–3.23), ApiDemos
+**2.80×** (2.66–3.09). Instrumentation confirms three versus one actual decoder
+invocations. These call timings include protocol/projection costs; they do not
+isolate the Java engine phase. NewPipe's whole raw token estimate increases
+951,332 → 962,330 with the default batch; ApiDemos decreases
+1,054,893 → 948,591. Fewer calls alone do not establish less context.
+
+## New selector: default batch versus table-only batch
+
+Three alternating pairs per APK; NewPipe repetitions 1/4/3, others 1/2/3.
+Repetition 4 replaces a refused start, described below. Both variants still
+perform one decode and return the same required facts.
+
+| Target   | Resource call, s | Whole elapsed, s |  Whole CPU, s | Family peak, MiB |
+| -------- | ---------------: | ---------------: | ------------: | ---------------: |
+| newpipe  |      9.18 → 9.35 |    23.95 → 24.85 | 23.65 → 23.82 |  1327.5 → 1323.6 |
+| apidemos |      6.46 → 5.81 |    23.28 → 19.79 | 22.90 → 19.47 |  1247.8 → 1197.0 |
+| settings |      4.21 → 4.06 |    17.66 → 19.39 | 17.42 → 19.04 |  1191.6 → 1122.4 |
+
+There is no consistent latency or whole-family memory improvement established
+for the selector. NewPipe and Settings have higher whole-task elapsed and CPU
+medians. Elapsed ranges overlap: NewPipe 23.53–34.46 → 21.59–42.80 s;
+ApiDemos 18.55–27.07 → 19.25–25.96 s; Settings 16.55–23.39 → 16.14–21.72 s.
+The cause of this variation was not established; a passing or faster run does
+not explain a slower one. The selector's supported benefit is reduced duplicate
+delivery, with its full task costs retained here.
+
+Full resource reply bytes fall 680,188 → 506,481 for NewPipe,
+616,841 → 463,588 for ApiDemos and 38,725 → 34,199 for Settings.
+
+Offline `tiktoken` 0.12.0 / `cl100k_base` estimates count one complete catalog
+page-array plus every call name/argument/reply, including inspection and close.
+Full replies include both textual and structured copies. Text-only replies are
+also counted separately. These are serialization estimates, not actual model
+usage; initialization/framing, prompts, client filtering/rendering/replay and
+continuations are unmeasured.
+
+| Target   | Text reply tokens | Whole raw transport tokens | Whole estimated reduction |
+| -------- | ----------------: | -------------------------: | ------------------------: |
+| newpipe  |   73,661 → 55,797 |          962,330 → 924,352 |                     3.95% |
+| apidemos |   65,693 → 49,162 |          948,591 → 913,693 |                     3.68% |
+| settings |     4,387 → 3,942 |          814,859 → 814,029 |                     0.10% |
+
+Discovery still has 207 tools; only `decode_android_resources` changes.
+The added schema costs 557 catalog bytes / 113 estimated catalog tokens
+(805,217 → 805,330). Raw discovery dominates this transport estimate; it does
+not establish what a client supplies to its model. Smaller replies and these
+estimates do not prove an actual agent context or investigation advantage.
+
+## Verification, attempts and limits
+
+- 94 source tests: provider/resource projection/service, including alias reads,
+  aggregate output exhaustion, malformed/physical failures, partial facts,
+  cancellation and cleanup. The table-only capacity, single-table provider
+  and CLI cases fail on the old implementation (three selected failures,
+  82 unrelated tests skipped).
+- Nine compiled CLI/MCP tests: schema conversion/advertisement, option forwarding,
+  Evidence parameters, legacy locale grammar and existing boolean choices.
+- 36 completed real MCP tasks and three real CLI tasks. Nine exact projection
+  oracle pairs; three legacy full-reply comparisons; alias/missing, single-table
+  and omitted-string cases pass. CLI normalized data, subjects and Evidence IDs
+  match MCP exactly on all three APKs.
+- `check:fast`, `build:cached` and `verify:test-discovery` passed; the last
+  discovered all 1,579 test files exactly once. `npm run check` and `npm run docs:check` also passed.
+- An authored test group initially exceeded the 150-line lint limit (153).
+  That gate failed after 189.31 s / 186.19 CPU s, peak 4,487,798,784 bytes;
+  build/compiled checks did not run in that attempt. The capacity test was moved
+  out of that group, and the complete corrected gate passed after 343.97 s /
+  338.67 CPU s, peak 4,311,293,952 bytes. No rule was disabled.
+- `projection-newpipe-after-2` was refused before scope/payload creation because
+  host availability was below 16 GiB; a following poll showed about 10.5 GiB.
+  It has no payload timing/counters and is not a completed measurement. The
+  refusal stays recorded; a fresh whole repetition-4 pair ran after recovery.
+  No existing receipts were overwritten and resource thresholds were unchanged.
+
+Raw transcripts, native outputs, intermediate failures and per-request workspace
+arguments remain in ignored local audit storage; the committed JSON is a curated
+summary. Small Settings resources and negative time results are retained.
+Actual models, APK execution, other providers/platforms and general complex
+software effectiveness were not verified by this checkpoint.

+# Linux Hopper embedding-runtime qualification
+
+This follow-up to the [string-record audit](hopper-string-records.md) resolves
+[#5015](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/5015): a successful package install
+could leave Hopper unable to start its Python bridge. This is a prerequisite
+correctness fix. It does not establish faster equivalent investigations.
+
+## Reproduction and owning correction
+
+Baseline REA `093ce695f0a7c3407c7fde520ed8b20c0981b408` ran the actual public
+`rea setup --yes --install-hopper --format json` in a fresh Ubuntu Base root,
+with full Linux UID/GID support, successful strict APT metadata refresh,
+default APT recommendations and unchanged vendor post-install scripts. Setup
+reported `ready` and `installed_hopper`; `dpkg --audit` was empty. Python 3.12
+was configured, but its reported `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libpython3.12.so.1.0`
+was absent. The signed Hopper package did not declare this dependency.
+
+An actual public MCP control-ELF workflow then timed out at its selected
+30-second startup budget. Installing only `libpython3.12` resolved to
+`libpython3.12t64` version `3.12.3-1ubuntu0.17`: one new package, no upgrades or
+removals. The unchanged REA runtime and target then completed all 13 calls.
+The independent earlier bootstrap dialog and controlled package intervention
+support the embedding-dependency diagnosis; timing alone does not.
+
+The shared Linux installer now asks `/usr/bin/python3` for its version and
+shared-library location after the original package transaction. It attempts an
+actual load. For a missing standard Ubuntu ABI/layout it installs the matching
+versioned library and verifies loadability again. APT success alone cannot
+establish readiness. Unknown metadata, alternate prefixes and alternate SONAMEs
+retain an explicit unknown diagnosis instead of guessing a package.
+
+Doctor consumes the same fresh, bounded producer, retaining both private-display
+and Python observations. Its Python facts concern the system interpreter;
+the interpreter actually selected inside Hopper remains unknown. The query
+uses isolated Python mode, disables site hooks and bytecode writes, has a
+10-second work deadline and 64-KiB output bound, and is not cached: package/interpreter
+changes must be visible immediately. The approval plan discloses the conditional
+package change without returning the probe program. Existing MCP analysis
+contracts and Evidence semantics are unchanged.
+
+Cancellation prevents starting another install stage and preserves the original
+reason. A running package transaction is allowed to settle, avoiding forced
+interruption of dpkg. This qualifies the install API's signal behavior through
+boundary tests; it does not claim new CLI interrupt plumbing or actual
+interruption of a real package transaction.
+
+A review follow-up preserves cancellation through doctor as well. A cancelled
+Python probe now raises the existing domain cancellation error with its original
+reason and completed private-display observations; the owned doctor workflow
+performs cleanup and attaches any cleanup failure. It no longer becomes an
+ordinary unknown diagnostic. The probe also opts into the existing
+stop-and-wait supervisor: cancellation and timeout wait for Python to exit,
+with the shared five-second grace period and forced-kill fallback. A real
+Python fixture holds its SIGTERM handler until the test releases it, checking
+that the probe retains ownership until exit. The success-path native measurements below precede
+this error-branch correction. Its boundary tests cover both successful cleanup
+and cleanup refusal; final-head validation is tracked on the PR. A pre-fix red
+execution and a final-head native rerun are not claimed.
+

+`0c70be0030f6bb821c4292c4f5b7f776b365c8ec`, based on main
+`23f984b1a884baefc3c44e4ab697f6eff61dffb6`.
+The measured runtime and bridge manifest covers 1,733 regular files, 26,537,393
+bytes. Its SHA-256 is
+`8800edc8e70965ae2132e57ca6d999ba276503f27f1045b33305c83cd0e2ff2a`
+(sorted paths, compact sorted-key JSON records containing path, bytes and

+## Actual workflows and measurements
+
+The accompanying [receipt](hopper-linux-python-runtime.json) preserves native
+stage outcomes, elapsed time, CPU time, peak memory, cleanup and token-estimate
+scope, including failed and stopped attempts. Installation uses root inside the
+owned fixture. Final analysis also uses a normal UID 1004 with a separate home
+and the authenticated public publisher evidence copied unchanged into that
+user's cache; production verification still checks it. No target was executed
+or modified. Non-root package installation through real pkexec authorization,
+custom Hopper Python configuration, native Debian installation and other
+operating systems remain unverified.
+
+Fresh final setup reported `ready` / `installed_hopper`, installed the matching
+shared library, left `dpkg --audit` empty and passed actual public doctor.
+Final normal-user sessions completed the positive, repeated, negative and
+decompilation checks: 19 `sqlite_master` matches in 1,437 recognized strings,
+74 broader `sqlite` matches and the expected version constant. Both CLI runs
+matched their MCP facts and Evidence identity; both target files stayed unchanged.

+Each control MCP session includes discovery and 13 calls: open, status, first
+literal query, six repeats, absent query, procedure listing, decompilation and
+close. SQLite uses 16 calls: a known exported address avoids a separate name
+lookup, and full native string inventory, broader query, regex, case and absence
+checks are included. Applicable returned string bytes are checked against the
+file. Warm queries must preserve facts and Evidence ID. CLI searches compare
+normalized facts and Evidence ID with their corresponding MCP result. Both
+target digests are checked after the task.
+
+“Fresh” means a new installation state or Hopper process, as indicated; OS
+caches were not flushed. Installation fixtures preload 247 previously fetched
+APT archives (138,023,324 bytes) without installing packages. These are not
+cold-network benchmarks. The baseline failure and successful repair are
+different outcomes, not a paired speedup. This change adds no analysis cache
+and makes no token reduction or complex-investigation advantage claim.
+
+Native stages have a 6-GiB container cap, 5-GiB early stop, no swap, 128 tasks,
+one CPU and explicit affinity. Their separate controller has a 512-MiB cap,
+no swap and 64 tasks. Native plus controller caps total 6.5 GiB. Heavy tasks
+run serially; admission waits for at least 16 GiB host availability and aborts
+below 8 GiB. Host build/check stages have an 8-GiB cap and 7-GiB early stop.
+No other user's processes were signalled.
+
+Native CPU and kernel memory peaks include the container guardian and observer.
+Payload-exit observations verify no analysis children remain before stopping
+the container. Controller counters are separate partial snapshots; adding
+separate peaks is only an upper bound, not a simultaneous measurement. Shared
+Docker daemon, containerd and system-manager costs and final counters after
+scope removal are unknown. Stopped attempts without payload-exit observations
+retain unknown cleanup/counter fields. Observed zero OOM counters at payload
+exit are not a claim about the whole host.

+## Failed attempts and limits
+
+- A single-ID namespace could not apply the real vendor/package UID/GID
+  ownership changes. It did not qualify a successful installation.
+- An inherited container-loopback proxy prevented publisher downloads; the
+  fixture was corrected to forward the same configured proxy through the
+  owned bridge gateway. No global proxy configuration was changed.
+- An early APT refresh exited zero with failed-index warnings. It was not
+  counted as a successful refresh; the strict clean run establishes the result.
+- One earlier setup was stopped by the host-memory guard during unpacking.
+  Its interrupted package state was retained separately; clean fixtures were
+  used for the qualified baseline and final installations.
+- SQLite exceeded a caller-selected 30-second startup budget. With the normal
+  120-second budget the bridge started, but an initial `libc` positive oracle
+  failed: those `.dynstr` bytes were not a recognized Hopper string. The

+# Hopper literal search: reuse decoded records
+
+For [#5010](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/5010), the bridge now keeps
+the existing decoded records in its sorted search inventory and projects only
+matches. Previously, every positive literal search called `_string_inventory`
+again, sorting all native object addresses and building another complete map
+before selecting records. The value-only `_strings` representation and the
+intermediate match list have been removed.
+
+This removes repeated work at its owner. Three paired SQLite workflows found
+shorter warm queries, but **did not demonstrate an overall task speedup**:
+whole elapsed and CPU were worse. Token estimates were effectively unchanged; no memory
+improvement was established. The [curated receipt](hopper-string-records.json)
+keeps individual measurements, equality checks and failed attempts.
+
+## Representation and reuse boundary
+
+The existing `(id(document), kind)` search cache now holds references to full
+records rather than just their decoded values. The existing string-record
+owner still performs byte decoding, encoding inference and unknown handling.
+Matching reads `record.value`; output copies the selected record with its
+address, retaining native display, encoding/extent metadata and decoding
+failures. The original document lifetime and annotation invalidation apply.
+This does not add another cache or duplicate decoded payloads. Both CLI and
+MCP use the same bridge through the existing application workflow. Regex keeps
+its supervised worker implementation.
+
+The lookup remains a linear scan of recognized native strings. A complete
+inventory is still decoded for the first exhaustive search, and returned hits
+still consume output and retained Evidence. This change does not introduce
+pagination, broader binary string discovery or a new context contract.
+
+## Pinned real-provider scope
+
+Baseline: REA 6.7.0 at `c12d9eda87aa5a022ee7e18ea96d8d03bfd12e96`, Node
+24.18.0, Debian 12 x86-64, Linux `6.1.0-53-cloud-amd64`. All paired tasks used
+the same compiled runtime SHA-256
+`0809b5004f214efa4b79775d5fda796eaecf4ad5756c55ee3b9d7cf82d91b750`.
+Baseline and candidate bridge digests are recorded separately in the receipt;
+the baseline file was mounted read-only over the bridge for baseline runs.
+
+The official [Hopper 6.6.0 Linux demo package](https://www.hopperapp.com:443/downloader/public/Hopper-6.6.0-Linux-demo.deb)
+was authenticated through REA's production publisher verifier: 35,748,722
+bytes, SHA-256
+`59705e50f7ebf9104abe1e72ac3949bed1a8e43ec67a8c9510a1c5056c200d27`,
+primary signing fingerprint `7C2D73BAFAF5B9A710A69DA1A26DF815099B1BCD`.
+The extracted launcher digest was
+`b2271008fb82bf14cfae5c3644cdde2b11fc6804bd7c99d67032ec1b1942d53c`.
+Normal demo activation used an owned private Xvfb display.
+
+The host's glibc 2.36 could not satisfy this package's GLIBC_2.38 requirement.
+Analysis therefore ran in a user-mapped private Ubuntu Base 24.04.5 namespace
+with glibc 2.39, Qt6/X11 and embedded Python 3.12. The
+[rootfs archive](https://cdimage.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-base/releases/24.04/release/ubuntu-base-24.04.5-base-amd64.tar.gz)
+matched its official HTTPS checksum, SHA-256
+`e77b6f10c2590cef872b33ee9f635a0e3fd1f57fb074c0e52b5c7f56147a0c86`;
+its publisher signature was not independently verified. Related libraries were
+installed only into that private image. Actual `rea setup` and vendor package
+post-install scripts were not executed. Native Debian installation and other
+operating systems remain unqualified.
+
+| Artifact                             |     Bytes | Independent oracle                                       |
+| ------------------------------------ | --------: | -------------------------------------------------------- |
+| Small authored C ELF                 |    17,360 | Source `input * 7 + 13` and ELF symbol                   |
+| Source-built conformance ELF         |    22,584 | Fixture source, known literal bytes and symbol addresses |
+| Shipped Debian `libsqlite3.so.0.8.6` | 1,437,848 | GNU objdump: version function returns `3040001`          |
+
+Artifact digests, compiler and flags are in the receipt. No target was executed.
+The small ELF was a baseline setup/decompilation smoke test; the conformance
+ELF had baseline/candidate semantic and CLI/MCP checks. SQLite supplied the
+repeated performance cohort. A constant-return oracle does not establish
+whole-program correctness, ABI inference or complex-investigation effectiveness.
+
+## Completed task and correctness
+
+Each of three baseline/candidate pairs used a fresh Hopper process and the
+same public stdio MCP workflow, including catalog discovery and 17 tool calls:
+
+1. Open the SQLite copy and inspect `binary_session`.
+2. Search `sqlite_master` in case-sensitive literal mode, then repeat six times.
+3. Read `list_strings` as a full-inventory validation oracle; compare all
+   matching records, including their metadata, with the selected result.
+4. Check broader `sqlite` search, regex, case-insensitive and absent-pattern
+   queries against their expected native inventory scope.
+5. Resolve `sqlite3_libversion_number`, decompile it, check its constant against
+   independent objdump, and close the binary and MCP transport.
+6. Verify unchanged target bytes and cleanup of the owned process family.
+
+There were 1,437 recognized string objects, 19 `sqlite_master` matches and 74
+broader `sqlite` matches. Applicable decoded hit bytes were also checked
+against file contents. All 42 Evidence payloads across the three pairs matched
+on normalized and raw facts, identity, subject, provider/profile, authority,
+confidence, limitations, relationship coverage, locations and evidence links.
+Live environment observations were excluded from cross-session equality.
+
+The real conformance workflows each completed 70 public calls, including six
+expected errors. They exercised Unicode symbol identity, literal metacharacters,
+case/regex modes, annotation cache invalidation, typed string fragments,
+display escaping and source-byte checks using the existing real-provider
+verifier. CLI `fragment_tail` search returned the same normalized facts and
+Evidence ID as MCP on both revisions (2,293 stdout bytes each).
+
+Native recognition remains qualified: the full 4,120-byte source literal and
+some known UTF-8, ellipsis and Latin-1 literals were not recognized. Their file
+bytes were verified, while decoded native-object coverage remains unverified.
+The fragmented 549-byte source literal was recognized as separate objects;
+matching does not pretend to join those fragments. Escaped text and literal
+backslash-n were distinguished. Real UTF-16 provider decoding was not qualified;
+the focused boundary fixture covers that representation separately. Empty
+search results establish absence only within the native typed-object inventory.
+
+## Measurements
+
+Runs were serial and ordered B1/C1, C2/B2, B3/C3. C2 first stopped under the
+host memory guard; its separate completed retry supplies the C2 row. OS caches
+were not flushed. “Cold” means the first string query in a fresh provider;
+“warm” means six repeats within that provider.
+
+Medians across the three completed sessions per revision:
+
+| Cost                                     |    Baseline |   Candidate |
+| ---------------------------------------- | ----------: | ----------: |
+| Per-run median warm query                |   14.849 ms |   12.628 ms |
+| Six warm queries, total                  |  100.202 ms |   75.552 ms |
+| Whole SDK workflow                       |    86.583 s |    90.786 s |
+| Whole guarded workflow                   |    89.384 s |    93.630 s |
+| Family CPU at payload exit               |    88.333 s |    92.590 s |
+| Kernel family peak, including file cache | 1,438.4 MiB | 1,440.0 MiB |
+
+Warm-query medians were lower in all three pairs, although one baseline run
+was particularly variable. Whole guarded elapsed was about 4.7% worse and CPU
+about 4.8% worse. The first query accounted for 65.2–71.2 seconds on baseline
+and 72.3–77.5 seconds on candidate; that interval includes native preparation.
+Do not interpret this cohort as end-to-end acceleration or dismiss the
+unfavorable rows.
+
+A separate pair moved the **existing** `procedure_address` call before the
+first string search, keeping the same 17 calls and equivalent facts/Evidence.
+Most preparation cost then occurred in that unchanged lookup: 67.949 seconds
+baseline versus 94.358 seconds candidate, before the changed search path ran.
+The subsequent first string query took 329.254 versus 337.533 ms; total guarded
+elapsed was 89.096 versus 113.917 seconds. This locates substantial cost outside
+literal projection and preserves the negative whole-task result. It does not
+prove its cause, establish a cold-query improvement or justify pooling the
+reordered pair with the original cohort.
+
+## Resource and context accounting
+
+Every heavy task used an owned cgroup v2 family: 8 GiB hard limit, 7 GiB early
+stop, zero swap, one CPU quota and affinity, 192 tasks, 3,072 MiB Node heap,
+and one heavy job at a time. Host admission required 16 GiB available; tasks
+stopped below 8 GiB. Later long runs added admission at 24 GiB sustained for
+20 seconds without relaxing the family guard.
+
+Family counters include the namespace, native engine, MCP client/runtime,
+validation and cleanup, including charged file cache. SDK wall time includes
+catalog discovery and correctness assertions. Admission wait is outside the
+guarded time and recorded separately where available; older waits and outer
+guard/systemd costs were not measured. Payload-exit CPU, kernel memory peak,
+limit counters and owned cleanup were verified while an observer remained.
+Final counters after the scope disappeared remain unknown. Completed paired
+payloads observed zero memory-limit, OOM/OOM-kill and task-limit events.
+
+The unchanged catalog advertised 207 tools, 3,158,927 serialized bytes,
+SHA-256 `a1851aa1bfe3d72d6be6bec130519dbdfc1ee49288320cfac0144ced77755c61`.
+Offline tiktoken 0.12.0 `cl100k_base` estimates for every completed SQLite
+comparison were effectively unchanged (medians across three runs):
+
+| Serialization counted once                         | Baseline estimate | Candidate estimate |
+| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------: | -----------------: |
+| Full catalog page array                            |           805,330 |            805,330 |
+| Named tool requests                                |               361 |                361 |
+| Raw replies                                        |           259,809 |            259,811 |
+| Total above                                        |         1,065,500 |          1,065,502 |
+| Text reply blocks alone, overlapping the raw count |           126,832 |            126,833 |
+
+Whole raw estimates ranged from 1,065,496–1,065,500 on baseline and
+1,065,500–1,065,506 on candidate. The small variations include live environment
+observations; there is no context reduction.
+
+The full inventory and extra controls are validation overhead included in
+these totals. Raw replies may contain text and structured copies. Actual model
+usage, prompts, initialization/protocol framing, client filtering/rendering or
+replay and independent-oracle context were not measured. The receipt separates
+other tasks and the interrupted transcript's persisted lower bound; it does
+not count an unrecorded in-flight request or reply as observed. No model-token
+saving or agent-reasoning advantage is claimed.
+
+## Failed attempts and verification
+
+The receipt preserves setup, diagnostic, failed and completed costs separately:
+
+- Initial private-rootfs configuration failed on an unmapped package GID, then
+  on the harness PATH; ordinary pending configuration completed successfully.
+- One low-host-memory probe was refused before creating a payload.
+- The first MCP harness used a relative path, correctly refused by the public
+  input boundary. A later custom-runtime launch lacked libXtst6, which the
+  production dependency list already includes. Both were harness/setup errors.
+- Two unchanged-baseline launches timed out at bridge startup. An owned-display
+  observation showed completed native analysis but a Python bootstrap failure.
+  Adding only the missing embedded Python library made the baseline pass;
+  [#5015](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/5015) records the separate
+  installer dependency hypothesis and its unverified actual-installer scope.
+- C2 stopped after 82.607 seconds when host available memory crossed the
+  unchanged stop threshold. Its sampled family peak was 1,517,019,136 bytes
+  and last observed CPU 78.255 seconds. Payload-exit/final counters are unknown;
+  it is incomplete and excluded from completed-run statistics.
+- An initial `test:local` invocation rejected built boundary projects before
+  running tests. The documented `test:focused` invocation then passed all
+  35 tests in five files, covering string search, regex, bridge facade and
+  real-provider verifier behavior. Those local tests do not themselves qualify
+  a native engine; the public native workflows above provide that evidence.
+
+`npm run check:fast` also passed (typecheck and lint both cached). Build and
+metadata preparation passed before the native workflows. `npm run docs:check`
+passed its cached metadata checks and all five README consistency tests.
+
+Reproduction uses `node scripts/rea.mjs --mcp` with an explicitly configured
+Hopper launcher and private display. Drive the named calls above with absolute
+target paths, retain full replies and compare independently verified bytes,
+facts and Evidence. For the source fixture, compile
+`tests/conformance/c/fixture.c` with
+`gcc -O0 -g -fno-inline -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fno-pie -no-pie`.
+Debug build paths can change rebuilt artifact digests. The shipped SQLite
+digest pins the measured artifact rather than every build of its package.
+
+The focused local gate was:
+
+```sh
+npm run test:focused -- \
+  tests/boundary/providers/hopper/hopperStringSearch.test.ts \
+  src/hopper/HopperRegexSearch.test.ts \
+  tests/boundary/providers/hopper/hopperBridgeFacade.test.ts \
+  tests/conformance/providers/hopper/realHopperSearch.test.ts \
+  tests/conformance/providers/hopper/realHopperExhaustiveSearch.test.ts
+```
